fixes.explanation: Yes, baker! The Lord says, "I will be a Father to you, and you will be My sons and daughters, says the Lord Almighty." A Father, with sons and daughters in the very same line. I know a thing or two about being called Papa, and it's the best name I've got.

Ooh, I'd flip that one back, friend! It's true. Paul quotes God saying, "I will dwell with them and walk among them, and I will be their God, and they will be My people." Dwell with them, walk among them: that's two promises in one breath. Nobody here is being told to wave at God from across the street.

False is right, baker! The Lord says, "Touch no unclean thing, and I will receive you." Turned away? Go look for it, because it's not in that line. The only door in that sentence is the one swinging open to receive them. I've been shut in a drawer, so believe me, I notice an open door.

Knowing things is great, friend, but that's not the word Paul uses here. He writes, "…let us cleanse ourselves from everything that defiles body and spirit, perfecting holiness in the fear of God." The word that fits the blank is holiness. Knowledge is a fine thing to carry into the kitchen, but it isn't what gets perfected in this verse.
